FAQ

How Talent Sheet works and where the numbers come from.

Who uses Talent Sheet?

Founders, investors, agents, brand teams and fans who want to see which athletes back, own or partner with which companies, and how those deals came together.

Where does the data come from?

Every deal links to the sources behind it: press releases, company and investor announcements, regulatory filings, and reporting from credible outlets. We do not copy from other deal databases.

What is the difference between Verified and Reported?

Verified means the deal is stated plainly by a reputable publication, a press release, a company announcement or the athlete's own announcement. Reported means the coverage is hedged (for example “reportedly” or a single unnamed source), or the only source on record is a lower-confidence one such as an aggregator or blog.

How fresh is it?

New deals are added as they are announced, and existing entries are corrected whenever a better source turns up.

What counts as an investment?

Any equity-linked relationship between a sports figure and a company: venture and angel investments, franchise ownership, brand deals that include equity, and executive stakes. A plain endorsement with no equity is listed as a partnership only when the athlete fronts a public campaign.

Which sports and industries are covered?

There is no boundary. Pro leagues, individual sports, Olympic athletes, coaches and team owners are all fair game, and companies range from consumer brands to sports tech, energy and fintech.
